scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

M-ESTIMATED-DISPUTE-SHARE.name: Share of disputed bills with ESTIMATED read type

M-RESPONSE-TIME.name: Dispute ticket response time vs SLA

F-03.statement: billing-db.tariff_change_log contains 0 records (no tariff changes logged).

F-04.statement: CRM dispute response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days.

F-06.statement: Field route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 9200 manual-read accounts for the 2026-08..09 period.

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request field dispatch route priority changes, which are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-08.statement: 320 accounts received an ESTIMATED read in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (sample account_id AC-20000, route R-00).

F-09.statement: Of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected by billing import validation with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION.

F-10.statement: Of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 56 had no AMI read received before cutoff and were not exported to billing (billing_import_status NO_READ_RECEIVED).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-FRAMING-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-response capacity/speed problem, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets would resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE-ERROR.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic errors in estimate substitution or acceptance of reads, producing wrong bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: Vendor-side AMI/MDMS export delivery degraded since August, causing missing accepted reads and estimate substitution that produced wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: The contracted manual meter-reading process (MeterWorks) degraded since August — e.g. late or incomplete routes — causing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-LEGITIMATE-BILL-INCREASE.statement: Bills issued since August are actually correct (e.g. higher measured consumption or tariff effects), and the 'surge' reflects customer disagreement rather than a billing-pipeline defect.

H-TARIFF-CHANGE-ERROR.statement: A tariff or billing-rule change around August produced billing errors on ACTUAL-read bills (not just estimated ones), contributing to the dispute surge independent of estimate substitution.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (billing_import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), causing estimate substitution for 1184/1240 (95%) of disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, independent of field route completion or vendor export delivery.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills, 1785 carry an ACTUAL read type and only 1240 carry ESTIMATED — a majority (59%) of disputes are not on estimated/substituted reads at all. This means estimate-substitution (AMI export failure or field-read failure) can at most explain the minority of disputed bills; some other cause must drive disputes on bills built from genuine reads.

E-01 still shows 1240 disputed bills carry read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 carry ACTUAL (59% majority ACTUAL) — that count split is unchanged. It no longer supports the premise that the ESTIMATED share stems from estimate-substitution for missing/unexported reads tied to route-completion shortfall: E-11 shows 95% of those same ESTIMATED-dispute bills had an accepted AMI read exported to billing but rejected for high consumption, not an absent read.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returns zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes are logged around the dispute-surge period. This rules out a tariff-rate change as the mechanism producing errors on bills, though it does not address billing import validation rule changes (a separate log, DA-RULES/billing-config).

CRM dispute_response_times (E-03) shows a 1.6-day median and 2.8-day p90 response time against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets — tickets are being answered well within SLA, not slowly. This undercuts the framing that the dispute surge is caused by a response-speed/capacity shortfall, since response latency is not elevated.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows ticket volume roughly flat (~600/month) in June-July 2026 then jumping to 1180-1260/month in August-September 2026 — confirming the surge is real and timed to August as claimed, but this says nothing about what is causing the wrong bills or why response is slow.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's uncorroborated statement that there has been no tariff change this year agrees with the already-recorded authoritative tool evidence E-02 (tariff_change_log empty), but as a non-authoritative stakeholder claim it adds corroboration rather than new fact weight.

route-log.route_completion_aug_sep (E-06) shows field manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts for the combined 2026-08..09 period — a real shortfall in route completion coincident with the dispute surge window. The record covers only Aug-Sep as one aggregate, so it cannot by itself show whether completion was higher before August (i.e. it confirms a below-target rate, not a confirmed drop since August).

E-06 still shows manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts for Aug-Sep — that rate observation is unchanged. It no longer means this shortfall is a confirmed contributing mechanism to the ESTIMATED-dispute population: E-11 shows 95% of ESTIMATED-dispute bills had an accepted AMI read exported and rejected on high-consumption grounds, so the route-completion shortfall does not explain the dominant share of ESTIMATED disputes it was credited with explaining.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims manual-read routes have run late since July due to being short three readers, causing those accounts to receive estimated bills. This is an uncorroborated stakeholder claim offering a mechanism consistent with E-06's below-target route completion, but no tool evidence yet confirms a staffing shortfall, and SH-FIELD has a stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing) to frame it this way.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is a document re-confirming the contractual basis (service contract §4.2) for the already-recorded constraint K-DISPATCH: the utility may request field dispatch route priority changes, but they are executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation. It establishes governance for any future route-change action; it says nothing about the root cause of billing disputes or route completion shortfalls.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-09) shows 320 accounts received an estimated read last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000/R-00); the record carries only account_id and route fields, with no read-type, tariff or import-status columns. It therefore cannot perform the segment analysis the work item intended, and since it is by definition about ESTIMATED-read accounts it does not touch the unresolved majority of disputes that carry an ACTUAL read type.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor engineer) claims via vendor ticket TX-4471 that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today, which, if true, would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query needed to test H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE. This means the ESTIMATED-dispute population is overwhelmingly AMI-channel and driven by a billing-import rejection rule rather than by vendor export failure, and does not obviously involve the manual-read route-completion shortfall the root problem attributed it to.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What is causing the majority of disputed bills (59%, ACTUAL read type) to be disputed, given no tariff change (E-02) and that estimate substitution does not apply to them?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any billing-pipeline fix (e.g., import validation rule rollback) is even applicable; without this, no automated or manual bill-fix action can be scoped safely.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query billing-config billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes coincident with August.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Do not propose or authorize any bill-adjustment or billing-rule fix until this log has been examined; keep scope to investigation only.

U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-BASELINE.question: Did manual-read route completion actually drop since July/August, or was 0.88 already the pre-existing rate (E-06 only covers the Aug-Sep aggregate)?
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-BASELINE.decision_impact: Determines whether a field-staffing/dispatch intervention is warranted as a timed fix versus an unrelated pre-existing condition.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-BASELINE.resolution_path: Query route-log for pre-August (Jun-Jul) completion rates to compare against the 0.88 Aug-Sep figure.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-BASELINE.safe_placeholder: Do not attribute the August timing of the surge to a staffing shortage without a pre-August baseline comparison.

U-AMI-EXPORT-STATUS.question: Is AMI/MDMS export delivery (vendor-side) degraded in a way that contributes to estimate substitution, given the mdms-export tool is DEGRADED and a HOLD was issued for ACCESS_PENDING?
U-AMI-EXPORT-STATUS.decision_impact: Determines whether a vendor-side AMI export fix is part of the remediation scope, versus the pipeline being limited to field reads and billing rules.
U-AMI-EXPORT-STATUS.resolution_path: Escalate vendor-provisioned export access for mdms-export (DA-MDMS) and re-query read event logs once access is granted.
U-AMI-EXPORT-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI export status as unresolved; do not rule in or out AMI-side causes until vendor access is provisioned.
U-AMI-EXPORT-STATUS.resolution: E-11 shows that for disputed ESTIMATED bills, vendor export to billing succeeded for 1184/1240 (95%) of cases (exported_to_billing=true, rejected downstream at billing import); only 56 (5%) show no read received/not exported, indicating AMI/MDMS export delivery degradation is not the dominant contributor to estimate substitution.

U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.question: Is a return of dispute ticket volume to the pre-August baseline (~600/month) a valid proxy for bills being correct, or could volume drop for other reasons (e.g., customer attrition, template changes) without the underlying cause being fixed?
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.decision_impact: Affects whether dispute_volume_monthly alone is sufficient as a success metric or must be paired with a bill-accuracy measure.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.resolution_path: Pair volume monitoring with a direct accuracy check (e.g., re-bill/credit rate or confirmed root-cause closure) rather than relying on ticket count alone.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.safe_placeholder: Report dispute volume trend as a leading indicator only, not as proof of root-cause resolution.

A-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTES.statement: The below-target route completion observed in Aug-Sep (E-06) is assumed to be a genuine contributor to the ESTIMATED-bill disputes rather than coincidental, though the record is an aggregate for Aug-Sep only and does not show a pre-August baseline.

A-STAFFING-CAUSE-UNCONFIRMED.statement: SH-FIELD's attribution of route lateness to a staffing shortfall since July (E-07) is treated as an unconfirmed claim, not fact, given SH-FIELD's stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and lack of corroborating tool evidence.

A-RULE-CHANGE-UNVERIFIED.statement: It is assumed the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) may hold the explanation for the majority ACTUAL-read disputes, but this has not yet been queried via billing-config.
